tools.name: python_status
tools.description:
Report which interpreter is in use and what it has installed.

    Start here when something looks wrong, and to find out whether the packages
    you need are actually present before relying on them.

tools.name: reset_namespace
tools.description:
Forget every variable, so the next call starts from nothing.

    restart_interpreter: also replace the interpreter process. Use this when it
        has become unresponsive, or when an imported module needs reloading
        from scratch.

tools.name: run_python
tools.description:
Run Python code and return what it printed. This is the main tool.

    Everything runs in one interpreter that stays alive between calls, so a
    DataFrame loaded in one call is still there in the next. Build an analysis
    up in steps rather than resending it whole.

    A final expression is shown the way a REPL would, so ``df.head()`` on its
    own displays the frame without print().

    Failures report the exception and the line of your code that raised it, and
    do not disturb anything already defined.

    Plots cannot come back as text: draw the figure here, then call
    save_figure to write it to a file.

tools.name: describe_object
tools.description:
Summarise one object: its type, shape, dtypes and a peek at the values.

    Recognises the shapes that matter in practice -- a DataFrame shows its
    dtypes and head, a fitted model shows its summary -- so this is usually
    more useful than printing the object whole.

tools.name: get_value
tools.description:
Evaluate an expression and return the value as JSON.

    For numbers, strings, lists and dicts. Anything larger -- a DataFrame, a
    fitted model -- should be summarised with describe_object instead, or
    reduced in Python before being asked for.

tools.name: load_data
tools.description:
Read a data file into the session as a DataFrame.

    The reader is chosen from the extension: .csv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls, .dta
    (Stata), .parquet, .sav (SPSS) and .json.

    name: what to call it in the session. It stays there for later calls, so
        load once and work from it.
    sheet: which sheet, for spreadsheets. The first by default.

tools.name: save_data
tools.description:
Write a DataFrame to a file, creating any missing folders.

    The format follows the extension: .csv, .xlsx, .dta or .parquet.

tools.name: preview_data
tools.description:
Show a DataFrame's shape, column types, missing counts and first rows.

    Worth calling straight after loading: it catches a column read as text, a
    header row mistaken for data, and missing values, before any of those
    reach an estimate.

tools.name: summary_statistics
tools.description:
Descriptive statistics for the numeric columns, with skew and kurtosis.

    columns: a space-separated subset, or empty for all of them.

tools.name: correlation
tools.description:
A correlation matrix over the numeric columns.

    method: "pearson", "spearman" or "kendall".

tools.name: regression
tools.description:
Estimate a linear regression and show the full statsmodels summary.

    dependent: the column on the left-hand side.
    independents: the columns on the right, separated by spaces.
    robust: leave empty for ordinary standard errors, "HC1" or "HC3" for
        heteroskedasticity-robust ones, or "HAC" to allow for serial
        correlation as well.
    name: what to call the fitted model, so diagnostics can be run on it
        afterwards.

    Rows with missing values are dropped.

tools.name: regression_diagnostics
tools.description:
Run the standard residual battery on a fitted model.

    Breusch-Godfrey for serial correlation, White for heteroskedasticity and
    Jarque-Bera for normality, each reported with the null it tested and its
    p-value against alpha.

    A test that cannot run is named with the reason rather than dropped, so
    the summary never counts fewer tests than it appears to.

tools.name: unit_root
tools.description:
Test a series for a unit root and report its order of integration.

    Tests the levels, then successive differences, stopping at the first that
    is stationary.

    test: "adf" for augmented Dickey-Fuller, or "kpss". KPSS reverses the
        null -- it tests stationarity -- and the report says so.
    regression: "c" for a constant, "ct" to add a trend, "n" for neither.

    The order is a mechanical reading of p-values. Structural breaks,
    seasonality and short samples all mislead these tests.

tools.name: plot
tools.description:
Draw a chart from a DataFrame.

    kind: "line", "scatter", "hist", "box" or "bar".
    x, y: column names. For line, hist and box, y may list several columns
        separated by spaces; leave it empty to use every numeric column.
    path: save straight to this file. Left empty, the figure stays open and
        save_figure can write it afterwards.

tools.name: save_figure
tools.description:
Write the current matplotlib figure to a file.

    path: destination; the extension picks the format (.png, .pdf, .svg).
        Missing folders are created.
    close: close the figure afterwards, so the next plot starts clean.

    Draw the figure with run_python first; this saves whatever is open.
